result.summary: Implemented the design at lib/letflow/design/iss0721-entity-event-type-seeding.md exactly, in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex. 1) replay_migrations/2's @spec gained a one-line addition to its error union: `| {:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, term()}}`, joining the existing `{:error, :tenant_not_provisioned}` / `{:error, {:migration_failed, Exception.t()}}` members. 2) replay_migrations/2's with-chain gained a second `:ok <-` clause: `with :ok <- maybe_seed_platform_event_types(using_default_manifest?, tenant_id), :ok <- maybe_seed_entity_event_types(using_default_manifest?, schema_name) do {:ok, applied_versions} end` -- reusing the existing using_default_manifest? and schema_name bindings, no new values threaded in, still inside the existing try/rescue so the migration_failed rescue clause is unchanged. 3) Added new private maybe_seed_entity_event_types/2, placed immediately after maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2 (directly below its closing `end`), with @spec `(using_default_manifest? :: boolean(), schema_name :: String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, term()}}` and two clauses: `maybe_seed_entity_event_types(false, _schema_name), do: :ok` (no-op gate, mirrors sibling) and `maybe_seed_entity_event_types(true, schema_name)` which calls `Letflow.Entities.EventTypes.seed!(schema_name)` and normalizes `{:ok, _seed_result} -> :ok` / `{:error, reason} -> {:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, reason}}` per design section 3. No idempotency handling added in this function per design section 4 (seed!/1 already tolerates duplicates internally). Used the fully-qualified `Letflow.Entities.EventTypes` call rather than adding a new module alias, since none existed and the design didn't call for one. Diff shape: three additions only (1-line @spec addition, 1-line with-chain clause addition, one new ~15-line private function block) -- no other lines touched, no scope creep. `mix format lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex` ran clean (no diff beyond what was already written matching project style). `mix compile` output: `Compiling 20 files (.ex)` with no warnings or errors -- clean compile, no new warnings introduced.
